sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Protein expressed and detected in HEK293T cells (western blot, L1/L2); C-terminal-tagged full-length ITM2B localises to cell surface retraction fibres and migrasomes (fluorescence imaging, L4). No functional assay reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: ITM2B is a single-pass type II membrane protein: residues 1–54 are intracellular, 55–75 are TM, and 76–266 are extracellular. The C-terminus (residue 266, Ser) therefore faces the extracellular space, 191 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. L1 explicitly engineers an HA tag at the C-terminus of full-length, membrane-anchored Bri2 in HEK293T cells; L4 independently places mCherry at the same C-terminal position and confirms surface localisation by migrasome imaging. Python verification: seq[265]='S', seq[264]='C', distance from TM end = 266−75 = 191. Full-length Bri2 (ITM2B) with a C-terminal HA tag (pcDNA3-N-Strep-Bri2-HA) expressed in HEK293T cells; protein detected by western blot. L4 (same paper series) further shows a C-terminal mCherry fusion on full-length ITM2B localises to the cell surface (retraction fibres/migrasomes) by fluorescence imaging.

literature_notes: Only one extracellular tag site is supported by the ledger. L1/L2 ground a C-terminal HA tag on full-length ITM2B; L4 corroborates with a C-terminal mCherry fusion showing surface display. The N-terminal Strep tag (L1/L2) and N-terminal GFP fusions (L3/L4) are intracellular because residues 1–54 are cytoplasmic; these are recorded in other_positions. No internal extracellular-loop insertions are reported in any ledger line.

literature_other_positions.note: N-terminal Strep tag on full-length Bri2 (pcDNA3-N-Strep-Bri2); residues 1–54 are intracellular, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface site.

N-terminal GFP fusion (GFP-ITM2B and GFP-ITM2B 1-115) expressed in cells; the N-terminus (residues 1–54) is intracellular, so GFP faces the cytoplasm despite the protein localising to surface migrasomes.
